逃.meaning: A fortune-teller cracks open a shell and reads a terrible <part>portent</part>: 'Tomorrow, the taxman visits.' That night he greases the <part>ramp</part> to his front door with butter. The taxman steps on it and slides all the way back to the street, while the fortune-teller climbs out the back window. A perfect <kanji>escape</kanji>.
逃.on: Climbing out, he scrapes his big <sound>toe</sound> on the window frame but doesn't stop.
逃.kun: He bangs his <sound>knee</sound> on the garden fence and keeps on running.

移.meaning: A farmer stacks <part>many</part> sacks of <part>grain</part> on the left side of his boat, and it tips. He drags them all to the right: it tips the other way. All night long, grunting and sweating, he has to <kanji>shift</kanji> them back and forth.
移.on: An <sound>ee</sound>l in the river watches, giggling every time the boat leans.
移.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>ps,' he says, as a sack splits and the dust makes him sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'

談.meaning: Two dragons meet in a little café, and every word of their <part>speech</part> comes out as a puff of <part>flame</part>. The menu catches fire, then the curtains, then the waiter's hat. They keep chatting politely: they have so much to <kanji>discuss</kanji>.
談.on: Afterwards the owner locks them in a damp <sound>dun</sound>geon to cool off.

倒.meaning: A gang of rebels marches into the palace, hangs their hats on the royal <part>coat hook</part> and sits down on the throne. On the day of their <part>arrival</part>, the old king is out in his slippers buying milk. That's a quick <kanji>overthrow</kanji>.
倒.on: Coming home, the king stubs his <sound>toe</sound> on the locked palace gate.
倒.kun: Then he trips over a dropped <sound>ta</sound>co and falls flat: '<sound>Oh</sound>!'

与.meaning: An old queen turns a golden <part>faucet</part> in the palace wall, and out drips exactly <part>one</part> diamond. Her servants <part>wrap</part> it in silk and carry it to a farmer's daughter. It's a gift only a queen could <kanji>bestow</kanji>.
与.on: The girl sends back a thank-you pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt.
与.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' she gasped when it arrived, dropping her <sound>ta</sound>co in the mud.

八.meaning: Two skiers zoom down a snowy slope side by side, then one swerves left and one swerves right, carving tracks that spread apart like the numeral <part>eight</part>. At the bottom they count their bruises: <kanji>eight</kanji> each.
八.on: '<sound>Ha</sound>, <sound>chee</sound>se!' they shout, as a friend snaps a photo of their tracks.
八.kun: '<sound>Yup</sound>,' nods the instructor, counting them again on his gloves.
